calls.description: The capabilities to run, 1-10, each {provider, capability, options}. Results come back in the same order.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

tools.name: mcp__Firecrawl__alexandria_library_search
tools.description: Check /library/skills first for any business workflow (sales or meeting prep, prospect lists, competitor, market or financial research, monitoring): it holds your team's and Firecrawl's step-by-step instructions for these tasks; follow a matching one instead of improvising. `cat /library/skills/search/<a-few-words-from-the-task>` (joined by hyphens) ranks them, your team's first; cat the path to read one. Explore the Alexandria library: Firecrawl's catalogue of data providers that return typed, sourced records (companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more) as a read-only filesystem, using shell commands. Use this to find out whether a provider covers the data a task needs, and to read its contract before alexandria_library_read. Layout: /library/<category>/<provider>/<capability>.md, one file per capability holding its contract (when to use it, inputs, outputs, and the call to send); /library, each category folder and each provider folder has a README.md describing what is inside. Category folders: agriculture, ai-models, apps, automotive, community, companies, developer, digital-intelligence, education, energy, entertainment, finance, game-development, government, health, healthcare, jobs, knowledge, life-sciences, marketing, music, news, people, places, podcasts, political-science, real-estate, research, restaurants, shopping, social, software, sports, travel; `ls /library` shows any added since. Available commands: ls, tree, cat, head, tail, grep, find, wc, sort, uniq, cut, tr, sed, jq, xargs, with pipes. Typical starts: `ls /library`, `cat /library/README.md`, or `grep -ril "mortgage" /library`. A file path is the execute address: /library/finance/fred/series/observations.md is provider "fred", capability "series/observations". Recorded example responses are under /examples/<provider>/<capability>.json. Free; does not run providers.

tools.name: mcp__Firecrawl__firecrawl_find_tools
tools.description: Browse Alexandria data providers and workflows or read a selected contract. Alexandria covers companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more: typed, sourced records through published contracts. Prefer normal firecrawl_search for a data task; it already returns matching providers. Use this tool when the contract you need was not returned in full, to browse a category when search found nothing, or before scraping the same fields from several pages. Discovery is free. Use query for semantic discovery or urls to find providers for a website. With no arguments, browse categories, then providers and tools. Contracts describe the inputs and outputs for execution through firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body or alexandria_library_read. alexandria_library_search explores the same catalogue as files. nextTool identifies further discovery or pagination. Discovery does not execute providers. Use firecrawl_search when you also need web results.

schema.name: mcp__Firecrawl__firecrawl_find_tools
schema.description: Browse Alexandria data providers and workflows or read a selected contract. Alexandria covers companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more: typed, sourced records through published contracts. Use this tool when the contract you need was not returned in full, to browse a category when search found nothing, or before scraping the same fields from several pages. Discovery is free. Use query for semantic discovery or urls to find providers for a website. With no arguments, browse categories, then providers and tools. Contracts describe the inputs and outputs for execution through firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body or alexandria_library_read. alexandria_library_search explores the same catalogue as files. nextTool identifies further discovery or pagination. query.description: Semantic lookup of tools for the data you need. Selectors constrain the search.

providers.description: Values from each listed tool's `provider` field (e.g. "apps-apple-com"). Alone, lists that provider's compact tools; with capabilities, scopes them.

categories.description: Category IDs returned by an empty call. Lists providers by default.

groups.description: Optional group IDs for explicit group browsing.

tools.name: mcp__Firecrawl__firecrawl_search
tools.description:
Use this when you need current or specific information from the web: recent events, latest releases and versions, prices, people and companies, statistics, or any fact that may have changed since your training data or that you are not sure of. Returns ranked results with query-relevant highlights; each web result is a title, URL, and description. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. `includeDomains` and `excludeDomains` are mutually exclusive hostname filters; categories limit result types to `research`, `pdf`, `developer`, or `gov`.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`. It searches an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation, and returns the results in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`.

For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns results in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; authenticated sessions also have `firecrawl_gov_search` as the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law.

Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. On an authenticated session, tool matches describe available structured-data capabilities, not executed data. toolDetail: "compact" (default) returns only provider, capability and description; "summary" adds metadata; "full" includes their input and output contracts. alexandria_library_read or firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body runs a selected capability; alexandria_library_search or firecrawl_find_tools reads full contracts.

tools.name: mcp__Firecrawl__firecrawl_search_feedback
tools.description:
Records schema-validated quality feedback for a prior `firecrawl_search` UUID `searchId`. A `good` rating requires a valuable result or a valuable source, `partial` either of those or at least one `missingContent` entry, and `bad` at least one `missingContent` entry or a query suggestion; caps are 50 `valuableResults`, 50 `valuableSources`, and 20 `missingContent` entries.

Eligibility is limited to successful searches within the feedback age window. The record is idempotent per search ID. Eligible first feedback for a search can refund 1 credit; refunds are subject to the team's daily cap. The response reports whether a refund was applied, along with submission and daily-cap status.

Mark useful returned results in `valuableResults` as `{"source", "position"}` copied off the result. Groups are numbered from 1 independently, so `{"source":"web","position":1}` and `{"source":"news","position":1}` are different results. Be exhaustive — results you do not list are treated as not useful. Reserve `valuableSources` for useful URLs that were NOT among the returned results; never report one result in both fields.

## Google_Sheets

## MiLatexAI
MiLatexAI edits the signed-in user's real LaTeX projects: Overleaf projects over
Overleaf's Git integration, and GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or self-hosted Git
repositories. If the user has no project connected yet, just proceed with their
request: any file tool returns a secure link where they paste their Overleaf Git
token (never in chat), relay that link and ask them to come back. start_connect
gives the same link; prefer it over connect_project, which takes the token in
chat. add_project adds more projects. Refer to a project by its name;
list_projects shows the connected ones. On the free plan only one project is active at a
time: if a reply asks which project to keep, ask the user and pass their answer to
switch_project; it also switches to a paused project when the user asks. Whenever the user wants to
check, view, change, update, rotate, or revoke their Overleaf token, use
change_token (it returns a secure link; the token itself can't be shown in chat).
To add or remove projects, use manage_projects, or add_project with just a project
URL (no token needed). Every write (edit_file/write_file/delete_file/upload_file) commits and
pushes immediately and counts toward the monthly limit; reading files does not.
Before editing, read the file so edit_file's old_string matches exactly.
read_file is for text files (.tex, .bib, .sty); download_file is for images and
PDFs; copy_file copies any file between projects on the server without base64.
When a project holds more than one document, list_files shows the .tex files to
pass as tex. list_checkpoints and get_history give the commit ids that
project_diff, restore_file and tracked_changes_pdf take; checkpoint saves one.
When the user asks why their paper won't compile or why they're getting errors,
run check_compile to build it and get the exact LaTeX errors, then read the
offending file, fix the errors with edit_file, and check_compile again.
When the user says a table or figure "looks weird/off/strange", or asks you to
look at how it renders or to see a picture of it, use show_table or show_figure to
get an IMAGE of the actual rendered float, then fix it with edit_file. The server
does no semantic matching: if the user names the float in words rather than a
number, first read the document (get_sections / read_section) to find its number
or \label, then pass that to show_table/show_figure. An unknown reference just
returns the list of tables/figures to choose from. show_page compiles the whole
project and returns a full page: use it only when the user asks how the document
looks on the page or to diagnose a visual problem, not routinely after edits.
Figure Studio (Pro): commit_figure saves a matplotlib chart the user has approved
(its code must save figure.pdf). The server renders it in an isolated sandbox and
commits both the source and the rendered file, so every figure stays editable:
list_figures shows them; read figures/src/<name>.py, change it, and commit again.
Commits are real, so show the user the figure before committing when you can, or
right after with show_figure; commit_tikz returns the rendered diagram, so show it. Before editing an existing figure, check
list_figures: if it says the output changed after it was rendered (or both
diverged), the stored code no longer matches it, so ask the user which version
should win instead of regenerating from stale code.

URL (no token needed). Every write (edit_file/write_file/delete_file/upload_file) commits and
pushes immediately and counts toward the monthly limit; reading files does not.
Before editing, read the file so edit_file's old_string matches exactly.
read_file is for text files (.tex, .bib, .sty); download_file is for images and
PDFs; copy_file copies any file between projects on the server without base64.
When a project holds more than one document, list_files shows the .tex files to
pass as tex. list_checkpoints and get_history give the commit ids that
project_diff, restore_file and tracked_changes_pdf take; checkpoint saves one.
When the user asks why their paper won't compile or why they're getting errors,
run check_compile to build it and get the exact LaTeX errors, then read the
offending file, fix the errors with edit_file, and check_compile again.
When the user says a table or figure "looks weird/off/strange", or asks you to
look at how it renders or to see a picture of it, use show_table or show_figure to
get an IMAGE of the actual rendered float, then fix it with edit_file. The server
does no semantic matching: if the user names the float in words rather than a
number, first read the document (get_sections / read_section) to find its number
or \label, then pass that to show_table/show_figure. An unknown reference just
returns the list of tables/figures to choose from. show_page compiles the whole
project and returns a full page: use it only when the user asks how the document
looks on the page or to diagnose a visual problem, not routinely after edits.
Figure Studio (Pro): commit_figure saves a matplotlib chart the user has approved
(its code must save figure.pdf). The server renders it in an isolated sandbox and
commits both the source and the rendered file, so every figure stays editable:
list_figures shows them; read figures/src/<name>.py, change it, and commit again.
Commits are real, so show the user the figure before committing when you can, or
right after with show_figure; commit_tikz returns the rendered diagram, so show it. Before editing an existing figure, check
list_figures: if it says the output changed after it was rendered (or both
diverged), the stored code no longer matches it, so ask the user which version
should win instead of regenerating from stale code.

</system-reminder>

13	---
14	
15	# Architecture Spine — Meridian maintenance triage
16	
17	## Design Paradigm
18	
19	One deployable ASP.NET Core process, organised as ports and adapters. The domain and application core know nothing about HTTP, the database or any model provider; adapters plug in at the edges. A React single-page app is built to static files and served by the same process.
20	
21	| Layer | Project | Holds | May depend on |
22	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
23	| Domain | `Meridian.Domain` | Job, Message, Issue, Urgency, Category, JobEvent, state transitions, emergency rules | nothing |
24	| Application | `Meridian.Application` | Use cases (intake pipeline, review, escalation, attendance, metrics), ports (`ITriageModel`, `IOutbox`, `IClock`, repositories) | Domain |
25	| Infrastructure | `Meridian.Infrastructure` | EF Core + SQLite, stub and OpenRouter model adapters, simulated outbox, prompt files, seed data | Application, Domain |
26	| Web | `Meridian.Web` | REST API, background worker, composition root, serves the built SPA | all three |
27	| Client | `client/` | React SPA | the REST API only |
28	| Eval | `Meridian.Eval` | Eval runner over the labelled set | Application, Infrastructure |
29	
30	```mermaid
31	graph LR
32	  Client[client React SPA] -->|HTTP /api| Web
33	  Web --> Application
34	  Web --> Infrastructure
35	  Eval --> Application
36	  Eval --> Infrastructure
37	  Infrastructure --> Application
38	  Application --> Domain
39	  Infrastructure --> Domain
40	```
41	
42	## Invariants & Rules
43	
44	### AD-1 — The model sits behind one port [ADOPTED]
45	
46	- **Binds:** R7, R10, R22, RULE-11, RULE-12
47	- **Prevents:** model SDK calls spread through the code; a provider swap touching use cases.
48	- **Rule:** Only `Meridian.Infrastructure` talks to a model. Everything else calls `ITriageModel.PrepareAsync(TriageRequest, CancellationToken) → TriageModelResult`. Implementations: `StubTriageModel` (recorded responses, the default) and `OpenRouterTriageModel` (OpenAI-compatible chat completions), selected at startup: OpenRouter only when `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is set. The model id comes from config `Triage:Model`.
49	
50	### AD-2 — A versioned, validated output contract
51	
52	- **Binds:** R6, R7, R10, R22
53	- **Prevents:** code trusting free-form model text; two parsers with different ideas of the shape.
54	- **Rule:** The model must return JSON matching contract `triage.v1`: `issues[]` each with `summary_en`, `category` (enum), `urgency` (enum), `property_text`, `explanation`, `vulnerability_mentioned` (bool), `confidence` (`high|medium|low`), plus `language`. One validator in Application checks it. Invalid output gets one retry, then the issue becomes Unsure (R10). `TriageModelResult` carries the raw output, model id, prompt version, latency and token counts for the event log.
55	
56	### AD-3 — Deterministic code decides; the AI only proposes
57	
58	- **Binds:** R4, R5, R8, R9, R12, R17, RULE-2, RULE-4, RULE-5
59	- **Prevents:** the AI's proposal becoming a decision through a side door.
60	- **Rule:** The intake pipeline runs in this fixed order: store message → emergency rules → acknowledgement (template) → model preparation (20 s timeout) → urgency merge → follow-up matching → one job per remaining issue → contractor lookup → queue → escalation scheduled. Emergency rules, follow-up matching, contractor lookup, escalation and outbound text are plain C# with unit tests and no model call. A model failure skips only the preparation step (RULE-11).
61	
62	### AD-4 — Urgency only goes up, except by a person
63	
64	- **Binds:** R5, R9, RULE-2
65	- **Prevents:** a later step or a re-preparation silently lowering an emergency.
66	- **Rule:** `Urgency` is ordered `Routine < Urgent < Emergency`. The only automatic operation is `Job.RaiseUrgency(level, reason)`, which ignores a lower value. Lowering exists only as `Job.SetUrgencyByPerson(level, person, reason)`, called from the review use case, and always writes an event.
67	
68	### AD-5 — One write path; every change is an event
69	
70	- **Binds:** R14, R15, R22, R23, R24, RULE-10
71	- **Prevents:** state changing without a history row; metrics disagreeing with the job view.
72	- **Rule:** Jobs change state only through domain methods on `Job`, which append a `JobEvent` (type, UTC time, actor, payload JSON). The application layer saves the job and its new events in one transaction. `JobEvent` rows are append-only: never updated or deleted. The numbers page (R24) is computed from events only, never from current job fields.
73	
74	### AD-6 — The job lifecycle is a fixed state machine
75	
76	- **Binds:** R13, R14, R15, R19, R20, R21
77	- **Prevents:** a job reaching a contractor without approval; each feature inventing its own statuses.
78	- **Rule:** States: `Prepared → Approved → SentToContractor → Attended`, plus `Rejected` from `Prepared`. Escalation (`EscalationState: None | NotifiedRachel | NotifiedBackup | Acknowledged | Failed`) is a separate field, not a lifecycle state. Only `Approved` can move to `SentToContractor` (R15). Illegal transitions throw.
79	
80	### AD-7 — Tenant and contractor text is fixed templates
81	
82	- **Binds:** R16, R17, RULE-5, RULE-6
83	- **Prevents:** model text reaching a tenant; the gas message being reworded.
84	- **Rule:** Outbound text comes only from templates in `Meridian.Application/Templates` with placeholders for reference, address and category. The gas safety message is a constant. Model output is never interpolated into outbound text.
85	
86	### AD-8 — Outbound and notifications go through an outbox
87	
88	- **Binds:** R16, R18, R19, R20
89	- **Prevents:** sending code scattered across features; the demo needing SMS or email accounts.
90	- **Rule:** Every acknowledgement, staff notification and contractor message is written as an `OutboundMessage` row (channel, recipient, template id, body, status) through `IOutbox`. The first version's adapter only stores and displays them (simulated sending). A real sender replaces the adapter later.
91	
92	### AD-9 — Time comes from a clock port; all times UTC
93	
94	- **Binds:** R16, R18, R19, R21, R24, RULE-8
95	- **Prevents:** escalation and promise timers that cannot be tested; mixed time zones.
96	- **Rule:** Code reads time only from `IClock`. Stored times are UTC; the UI shows Europe/London. Working days are Monday to Friday. The 30-minute escalation and 24-hour promise are checked by one background worker every minute; each check is idempotent.
97	
98	### AD-10 — Data sent to the model is minimal and treated as data
99	
100	- **Binds:** R7, RULE-14, prd AI never-do list
101	- **Prevents:** tenant personal data leaking to the provider; instructions inside a message steering the model.
102	- **Rule:** The model receives the message text and received time only: no sender address or name field. The system prompt is a versioned file (`prompts/triage.v1.md`) and the message is wrapped as quoted data in the user turn. The allowed categories and urgencies are listed in the prompt and enforced by AD-2's validator, so an injected value is rejected.
103	
104	### AD-11 — Contractor links are capability tokens
105	
106	- **Binds:** R20
107	- **Prevents:** a contractor link that opens other jobs; needing contractor accounts.
108	- **Rule:** Each `SentToContractor` job gets a random, single-job token; the link marks only that job attended and expires when it is attended or rejected.
109	
110	### AD-12 — The eval runs through the real pipeline
111	
112	- **Binds:** prd SM-1, SM-7, AI behavior and evaluation
113	- **Prevents:** an eval that measures the prompt but not the rules and merge the product actually applies.
114	- **Rule:** `Meridian.Eval` loads `eval/cases/*.json` (message plus expected issues, category, urgency), runs each through the same Application pipeline with the configured `ITriageModel`, and writes `eval/results/<date>-<model>.json` and a Markdown summary. Errors are classed by harm: missed emergency (critical), wrong urgency up (tolerable), wrong category (minor).
115	
116	### AD-13 — Property and follow-up matching are fixed code
117	
118	- **Binds:** R7, R8, R11
119	- **Prevents:** two features resolving "14b Alder Court" to different properties, or grouping messages by different rules.
120	- **Rule:** The model returns only `property_text`. `PropertyResolver` normalises it and matches it against seeded properties; no match, or more than one, sets the job's property to unresolved and the job goes to the Unsure category for a person to pick. `FollowUpMatcher` attaches an issue to an existing job when the property is the same, the category is the same (or either is Unsure), the job is not `Attended` or `Rejected`, and the job was opened within the last 7 days; otherwise a new job is created.
121	
122	## Consistency Conventions
123	
124	| Concern | Convention |
125	| --- | --- |
126	| Naming | C# PascalCase; domain nouns exactly as in the PRD glossary (Message, Issue, Job, Follow-up, Urgency, Category). Events are past tense: `MessageReceived`, `RulesApplied`, `JobPrepared`, `JobApproved`. |
127	| Ids | Guid primary keys. Human job reference `MER-` + zero-padded sequence (e.g. `MER-000123`), shown to tenants. |
128	| API | REST JSON under `/api`, camelCase, DTOs in Web only (never return entities). Errors as RFC 9457 problem details. |
129	| Enums on the wire | Strings, not numbers. |
130	| Config | `appsettings.json` plus environment variables; secrets only from environment (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`). |
131	| Logging | `ILogger` structured logging; no message text or tenant data in logs (it lives in events). |
132	| Acting user | No login in the first version; the SPA has an "acting as" switch (Rachel, backup) recorded as the event actor. |
133	| Tests | xUnit; domain and application rules are unit-tested with `IClock` faked; one API test via `WebApplicationFactory`. |
134	
135	## Stack
136	
137	| Name | Version |
138	| --- | --- |
139	| .NET SDK / runtime | 8.0 (SDK 8.0.134) |
140	| ASP.NET Core | 8.0 |
141	| EF Core + SQLite provider | 8.0.34 |
142	| xUnit | 2.9.3 |
143	| Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing | 8.0.34 |
144	| Node.js (client build) | 22 |
145	| React | 19.3.1 |
146	| Vite | 8.3.5 |
147	| @vitejs/plugin-react | 6.1.2 |
148	| TypeScript | 7.0.2 |
149	| Model provider | OpenRouter, OpenAI-compatible chat completions API; stub by default |
150	
151	## Structural Seed
152	
153	```text
154	src/
155	  Meridian.sln
156	  Meridian.Domain/          # entities, enums, emergency rules, state machine
157	  Meridian.Application/     # pipeline, use cases, ports, validator, templates
158	  Meridian.Infrastructure/  # EF Core, model adapters, outbox, prompts/, seed data
159	  Meridian.Web/             # API, background worker, serves client build from wwwroot
160	  Meridian.Eval/            # eval runner
161	  Meridian.Tests/           # unit and API tests
162	  client/                   # React + Vite SPA, builds into Meridian.Web/wwwroot
163	eval/
164	  cases/                    # labelled eval cases (JSON)
165	  results/                  # eval run outputs
166	run.sh                      # one command: build client, run migrations and seed, start
167	```
168	
169	```mermaid
170	erDiagram
171	  MESSAGE ||--o{ ISSUE : "split into"
172	  JOB ||--|{ MESSAGE : "first plus follow-ups"
173	  ISSUE }o--|| JOB : "becomes or attaches to"
174	  JOB ||--o{ JOB_EVENT : "history"
175	  JOB }o--|| PROPERTY : "at"
176	  PROPERTY }o--|| BUILDING : "in"
177	  BUILDING ||--o{ CONTRACTOR_ASSIGNMENT : "usual contractor per category"
178	  CONTRACTOR_ASSIGNMENT }o--|| CONTRACTOR : ""
179	  JOB ||--o{ OUTBOUND_MESSAGE : "acknowledgements, notifications"
180	```
181	
182	```mermaid
183	sequenceDiagram
184	  participant T as Tenant message
185	  participant P as Intake pipeline
186	  participant R as Emergency rules
187	  participant M as ITriageModel
188	  participant Q as Review queue
189	  participant W as Background worker
190	  T->>P: store unchanged (R1)
191	  P->>R: evaluate (R4)
192	  P->>P: acknowledgement or gas message via outbox (R16)
193	  P->>M: prepare, 20 s timeout (R7)
194	  M-->>P: triage.v1 JSON or failure
195	  P->>P: merge urgency, match follow-ups, lookup contractor (R8, R9, R12)
196	  P->>Q: job Prepared, events written (R13, R22)
197	  W->>W: every minute: escalate emergencies, check 24 h (R18, R21)
198	```
199	
200	**Deployment and environments.** One environment for the assessment: local machine. `run.sh` (and `run.ps1` for Windows) installs client packages, builds the SPA into `Meridian.Web/wwwroot`, applies EF migrations to `meridian.db`, seeds buildings, contractors and the six forwarded messages, and starts the app on `http://localhost:5080`. No cloud hosting, containers or CI in the first version.
201	
202	## Capability → Architecture Map
203	
204	| Capability / Area | Lives in | Governed by |
205	| --- | --- | --- |
206	| R1–R3 intake | Application `IntakePipeline`, Web `/api/messages` | AD-3, AD-5 |
207	| R4–R5 emergency rules | Domain `EmergencyRules` | AD-3, AD-4 |
208	| R6–R7, R10 AI preparation | Infrastructure model adapters, Application validator | AD-1, AD-2, AD-10 |
209	| R8 follow-ups | Application `FollowUpMatcher` | AD-3 |
210	| R9 urgency merge | Domain `Job.RaiseUrgency` | AD-4 |
211	| R11–R12 contractor map | Infrastructure seed data, Application `ContractorLookup` | AD-3 |
212	| R13–R15 review | Application review use case, client queue page | AD-5, AD-6 |
213	| R16–R17 tenant messages | Application templates, `IOutbox` | AD-7, AD-8 |
214	| R18–R19 escalation | Web background worker, Application `EscalationService` | AD-6, AD-8, AD-9 |
215	| R20–R21 attendance | Application attendance use case, Web `/c/<token>` | AD-6, AD-9, AD-11 |
216	| R22–R23 events | Domain `JobEvent`, client job history | AD-5 |
217	| R24 numbers | Application `MetricsQuery` over events | AD-5 |
218	| Eval | `Meridian.Eval`, `eval/` | AD-12 |
219	
220	## Deferred
221	
222	- **Authentication and roles:** no login in the first version; the acting-as switch stands in. Revisit before any live use.
223	- **Real email intake and sending, SMS, WhatsApp:** adapters behind `IOutbox` and a new intake endpoint later (R3).
224	- **UK bank holidays in working days:** Monday to Friday is enough for the demo.
225	- **Hosting, CI, containers:** local run only for the assessment.
226	- **Data retention and protection rules (prd OQ-3):** open with the user and Meridian.
227	- **Which OpenRouter model (prd OQ-5):** chosen against the eval when the key is added.
228	- **Batching, caching, queueing for ten times the volume:** discussed in AI-DESIGN.md, not built.

34:Meridian's maintenance inbox is read by one person, so when Rachel is away nothing moves and out of hours nobody reads it at all, which breaks the 24-hour emergency promise in the tenancy agreement. This product reads every message the moment it arrives and prepares the job, so that whoever is on duty, Rachel or a backup who does not know the buildings, only has to check and approve.
46:**UJ-1. The Walshes' boiler on a Friday night.** Michael Walsh, with a 7-month-old at home, emails at 19:15: no heating or hot water since the morning, it is November. Within a minute he gets an acknowledgement with a reference. The fixed rules flag "no heating" in winter as an emergency; the job is prepared (heating, 14b Alder Court, the heating contractor, "Urgent because: no heating in winter, baby in the house") and Rachel's phone is notified. She is on holiday and does not acknowledge, so after 30 minutes Dawn is notified. Dawn opens the job, sees the explanation and the usual contractor, and approves. Michael's follow-up at 19:51 and his wife's email at 20:30 from another address are attached to the same job as follow-ups, not new jobs. The heating engineer marks the job attended the next morning, inside 24 hours. Failure: if Dawn does not acknowledge either, the job stays at the top of the queue marked as escalation-failed. Realised by FR-1, FR-4, FR-5, FR-8, FR-9, FR-13, FR-15, FR-16, FR-18, FR-20, FR-22.
61:- **Urgency**: emergency (24-hour promise, escalated at any hour), urgent (top of the next working day's queue) or routine (five working days).
69:- **Attended**: the contractor has been to the property. The 24-hour emergency promise is measured to this.
114:- **FR-21.** If an emergency job is not marked attended within the time left on its 24-hour promise, the on-duty person is alerted to send the fallback contractor.
119:- **FR-24.** The MD can see a numbers page: jobs by category and urgency, time from message to first human look, time to approval, time to attendance, and how often the 24-hour and five-day promises were met.
130:- **RULE-8.** Promises: emergency, a contractor attends within 24 hours of the first message; routine, within five working days.
159:- **SM-3. 24-hour promise kept** on every emergency job, measured to attended. Validates FR-20, FR-21.

content.text:
The attendance story is implemented as the plan specifies, except for one open conflict in the overdue alert (see below). Nothing is committed.

**What changed**
- **Domain:** `Job.Attendance.cs` adds send, resend, mark attended, overdue, and the token hash. Three events (`SentToContractor`, `JobAttended`, `AttendanceOverdue`) are appended at the end of `EventType`.
- **Application:** approval now sends the job to its contractor in the same unit of work. New use cases: `GetContractorJob`, `MarkAttended`, `ResendToContractor`, `CheckOverdueAttendance`. Templates and token helpers are in `Attendance/`. The queue puts overdue jobs first.
- **Infrastructure:** `ContractorAttendance` migration (token hash unique, sent-to contractor, attended time, overdue flag). Two repository lookups.
- **Web:** `AttendanceEndpoints.cs` has the GET and attended endpoints and the resend endpoint. The escalation worker runs the overdue check each minute.
- **Client:** `/c/<token>` contractor page with "Mark attended". Staff see the contractor link in the job detail. The queue has an overdue alert with a fallback picker and resend. Contractor messages no longer appear under "Sent to tenant".
- **Tests:** four existing approval tests now expect the job to end at `SentToContractor`. The matrix rows are covered by 24 new tests.
- **Plan file:** ticked the six execution items and added Implementation Notes (outside the frozen block).

**Verification**
- `dotnet build -warnaserror`: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `dotnet test`: 549 passed, 1 skipped (baseline was 525 passed, 1 skipped). New: 10 domain, 7 application, 7 API.
- `npm run build`: passes.
- Smoke run against a scratch DB: `/c/<token>` serves the SPA, and bad tokens return 404.

**Left incomplete or risky**
- **Overdue alert returns after a resend (needs a decision).** The plan says resend clears the overdue flag, but overdue is measured from the first message (RULE-8). The next worker minute therefore raises the alert again for a resent job. I followed the plan literally. The options are to measure from the latest send or to keep the flag on resend.
- **Signature deviation.** `SendToContractor` and `ResendToContractor` take an extra outbound id argument, because the `SentToContractor` event must record it.
- **Jobs approved before this change stay `Approved`.** They are not sent and there is no backfill.
- **Client not checked in a browser.** The contractor page and the overdue alert were type-checked and built, but not viewed.
